title: The Protocol of the Green Zone
premise: Marguerite Kavanagh built a quiet life erasing problems for the Meridian Group, an embassy that appears on no map, until a dead handler's voiceprint unlocks a server in Tbilisi and reveals she was not recruited into the network—she was manufactured by it, one of a dozen 'graduates' of a behavioral engineering program called the Green Zone Protocol. Hunted by the colleagues she once called family and shadowed by a journalist who has the other half of the archive, Marguerite must decide whether loyalty to the people who made her outweighs the truth of what they made her for. As the Geneva summit approaches and the network prepares to activate its remaining graduates, she burns the Protocol from the inside, trading her anonymity and her last illusion of a self that existed before the training. In the end she walks out of the ashes with no name the world will recognize, but for the first time, one that is entirely her own.
about_author: Cyrus Dunmore is the pen name of a former logistics contractor who spent a decade in cities that appear on no itinerary, writing at night in notebooks he no longer possesses. He lives near water, under a name he chose himself, and this is his second novel.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: Marguerite Kavanagh's POV. A routine cleanup job in Vienna—a missing diplomat, a sanitized hotel room—shows her precision and her insomnia. She flinches at a voice on a phone that resembles her dead handler, Aldous Wren. Emotional beat: competence masking dread; the reader senses she is already broken in a way she hasn't admitted.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A dead-man's switch triggers: Wren's voiceprint unlocks a server in Tbilisi and pushes a fragment of an archive to her private terminal. The file names her—not her cover identity, her real one, which she believed never existed. Emotional beat: vertigo; the ground of her identity cracks open.

chapters.title: Meridian House
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She returns to the embassy-that-isn't and lies smoothly to her superior, Deputy Director Ilse Marchetti, while cataloguing what's changed: new faces, new locks, a summons she deflects. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of deceiving the only family she has.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Doors
chapters.summary: Journalist Tomas Reyes's POV, first appearance. Reyes, who has chased rumors of a behavioral engineering program for six years, receives the other half of Wren's archive from a dying source. He recognizes Marguerite's alias in the files. Emotional beat: obsessive hope; a man who has sacrificed everything for a story he can barely prove.

chapters.title: Graduate Nine
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The archive fragment reveals the Green Zone Protocol: twelve children conditioned into deniable operatives, and Marguerite is Nine. She tests her own memories against the file and finds the seams—implanted recollections, a childhood that never happened. Emotional beat: grief for a self that was never real.

chapters.title: The Summons
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marchetti confronts her with the Tbilisi breach and offers a choice: help close it and be restored to favor, or be 'retired.' Marguerite accepts, planning to use her access to reach the full archive. Emotional beat: cold resolve; she chooses to become a double agent inside her own life.

chapters.title: Vienna Station
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Reyes flies to Vienna to intercept Marguerite and walks into a Meridian surveillance net. He escapes by the narrowest margin, aided by an anonymous warning he suspects came from Marguerite herself. Emotional beat: paranoid exhilaration; the hunt has become mutual.

chapters.title: What Aldous Knew
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Following Wren's dead-drop chain through Prague, she reconstructs his final months: he discovered the Protocol's next phase—activation of the remaining graduates during the Geneva summit—and was killed for it. Emotional beat: mourning converted to mission; Wren becomes her cause.

chapters.title: The Family That Trains You
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, flashback interleaved with present. A training memory surfaces intact: a green-painted room, a woman called Mother Voss, a test involving a lie Marguerite was made to tell until she believed it. Present-day Marguerite realizes her loyalty was installed, not earned. Emotional beat: the theme of loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Two Halves of a Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Marguerite and Reyes. They finally meet—hostage exchange of trust: her archive fragment for his. Merged, the files reveal the location of the remaining graduates and the Protocol's activation key. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two people who trust no one choosing to trust each other.

chapters.title: Graduate Four
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She tracks a fellow graduate, Daniel Okafor—now a respected Geneva security consultant—and finds him already activated, executing pre-summit positioning. He recognizes her, calls her by her childhood number, and lets her live with a message: come home. Emotional beat: horror and pity; the mirror of what she could be.

chapters.title: Marchetti's Confession
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marchetti, sensing the leak, tells Marguerite a half-truth: Meridian inherited the Protocol from its founders and Marchetti has been trying to contain it for years. Marguerite cannot tell if this is another installed lie. Emotional beat: the reader's trust in every character destabilizes.

chapters.title: The Green Room
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She infiltrates the Protocol's original facility in the Carpathians and finds Mother Voss, old and unrepentant, running the activation remotely. Voss offers Marguerite her 'real' file—her origin, her birth name—in exchange for walking away. Emotional beat: temptation; identity offered as a bribe.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. Meridian burns Reyes's life—sources, savings, bylines—and he goes underground with Marguerite. He publishes nothing, holding the story as leverage, which tortures him. Emotional beat: sacrifice tested; the journalist learns silence can be a weapon or a wound.

chapters.title: Counting Down
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Three days to the summit. She maps the activation chain: a voiceprint cascade, Wren's voice as the key, graduates positioned in three delegations. She realizes Meridian cannot stop it without exposing itself—and neither can she. Emotional beat: the trap closes; every option costs everything.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marchetti discovers Marguerite's double game but, instead of exposing her, proposes an alliance: burn the Protocol, protect Meridian's core. Marguerite must decide whether a loyal enemy is safer than a truthful friend. Emotional beat: uneasy pact; loyalty and truth finally forced into the same room.

chapters.title: Geneva, Day One
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The summit opens. Marguerite and Reyes run counter-positioning against the activated graduates while Marchetti feeds them Meridian access. Okafor corners Marguerite in a service corridor; she talks him down halfway before he vanishes. Emotional beat: high-wire tension; small victories that feel like losses.

chapters.title: Voice of the Dead
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The activation cascade begins. The only way to break it is to feed the system Wren's voiceprint herself—triggering the archive's final layer, which will expose Meridian along with the Protocol. Emotional beat: point of no return; she chooses truth over every remaining shelter.

chapters.title: The Protocol of the Green Zone
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, climax. In the summit's security nerve center, Marguerite speaks Wren's words into the cascade, collapsing the activation and flooding the world's feeds with the Protocol's archive. Voss's voice dies mid-sentence. Okafor, freed mid-task, shields her from a Meridian cleaner and is gravely wounded. Emotional beat: catharsis through self-destruction; she burns the network that made her and nearly burns with it.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Reyes's POV. The story breaks everywhere; Meridian dissolves into plausible denials. Marchetti disappears with a clean exit, owing Marguerite a debt she may never collect. Reyes publishes everything except Marguerite's name—the one act of loyalty he can still offer. Emotional beat: bitterswee vindication; truth won, but at the price of every institution that gave her purpose.

chapters.title: The Name She Chose
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Recovering in a Lisbon hospital, Marguerite reads her true origin file at last and finds it smaller and sadder than the myth: an ordinary child, taken ordinary-ly. She lets the file go, keeps Wren's lighter and Reyes's number, and picks a name for herself. Emotional beat: quiet rebirth; identity as choice, not inheritance.

chapters.title: A Door, Unlocked
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, coda. Months later, a woman with a familiar voiceprint pattern appears at Marguerite's door—Graduate Eleven, the last unaccounted graduate, asking not for rescue but for the truth. Marguerite opens the door. Emotional beat: resolution with an open edge; the cycle can be broken, one graduate at a time.
